question: Is the Aurzen TravelPlay a good back seat screen for a Tesla Model Y? Where can I buy one?
query: Aurzen TravelPlay review Tesla Model Y compatibility where to buy 2026

replays.text:
**It can be a good parked-car movie screen, but it isn’t an electronic display by itself**—you’ll need a compatible portable projector. It’s a foldable, clip-in screen and sunshade, with roughly 47-inch and 50-inch panels for rear-seat, roof, or tailgate viewing. Use it only while parked. [Aurzen’s product page](https://aurzen.com/collections/new-releases/products/aurzen-travelplay-autocinema-screen-for-tesla-model-y)

Fit is best for the **2025–2026 Model Y Refresh**. Aurzen says it can also work in **2020–2024 Model Ys** in roof mode, but the rear screen won’t fully cover the window—so check your model year before buying.

You can buy it from [Aurzen’s official U.S. store](https://aurzen.com/collections/new-releases/products/aurzen-travelplay-autocinema-screen-for-tesla-model-y), listed at **$119.99** in the search results. It’s a reasonable option if you want a portable projection setup; it’s not the right choice if you’re looking for a screen that works while driving or without a projector.

**It can be a good back-seat screen if you want a projector setup—not a plug-and-play video display.** TravelPlay is a foldable, clip-in projection surface with roughly 47-inch and 50-inch panels. It supports rear-seat, panoramic-roof and tailgate viewing, and doubles as a sunshade. You’ll need to provide a compatible portable projector, and it’s meant to be used **only while the car is parked**. For the clearest picture, use it in low light. ([Aurzen product page](https://aurzen.com/collections/new-releases/products/aurzen-travelplay-autocinema-screen-for-tesla-model-y))

**Check your Model Y year before buying:** it’s designed for the 2025–2026 refresh. Aurzen says it can work with 2020–2024 models in roof mode, but the rear screen won’t fully cover the window.

On **2020–2024 Model Ys**, it can work in roof mode, but the rear screen won’t fully cover the window. It’s **for use only when the car is parked**, so it won’t serve as an in-drive back-seat entertainment screen. If that suits your use, it looks convenient: tool-free clips, foldable panels, and a carry bag.
